fact: Burkina24 reports Orange Burkina Faso's Max It app, relaunched on 18 September 2026, offers Orange Money mobile money to subscribers of all networks, per Orange's Abdramane Diallo.
Burkina24 reports Max It is interconnected with almost all the country's banks for transfers between bank accounts and Orange Money accounts, per Orange's Abdramane Diallo.

Orange Money Burkina Faso's director general says the service has about 100,000 points of sale in the country, and SONAR Assurance signed a convention on 18 September 2026 to sell policies and take premium payments through it.

leFaso.net reports that the BCEAO's PI-SPI interoperable instant payment platform, launched 30 September 2025, connects banks, e-money institutions and payment institutions, with 80 connected by 24 June 2026.

Through PI-SPI, transfers in Burkina Faso run between banks, financial institutions and e-money operators, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week; nine institutions including Orange Money are authorised as of 24 February 2026.
PI-SPI lets funds move instantly between banks, e-money issuers, microfinance institutions and payment institutions, 24/7, by phone number or alias, per the BCEAO governor.
Wave mobile money is in use in Burkina Faso, with Wave and ANPFI running financial training in Ouagadougou, Bobo-Dioulasso and Banfora, per a Wave public policy director.
TechAfrica News reports Wave Money operates in five regions of Burkina Faso with over one million users, offering transfers, airtime and bill payments.
Orange Money Burkina Faso is an e-money service with over 11 million customers, per the article.
Orange Money and BSIC Burkina launched Bank to Wallet and Wallet to Bank transfers via *144# on 30 May 2025, linking BSIC accounts and Orange Money wallets in real time.
Tech Review Africa reports Telecel Money has an extensive user base in Burkina Faso and signed an agreement with GIEPHAB (2,500+ pharmacies) to accept its payments, starting in Ouagadougou.
Orange Money Burkina Faso, an operating mobile money service, announced on 5 March 2025 an upgrade of its mobile financial services platform to Comviva's Mobiquity Pay X, per We Are Tech Africa.
We Are Tech Africa reports Faso Arzêka payments can be made through Arzêka Money, mobile money, bank cards and bank transfers.
source_slug: 2025-01-30 Burkina Faso launches Faso Arzeka digital payment platform

fact: The Ministry says FASO ARZEKA lets users create an electronic wallet and is connected to bank cards, mobile money and bank transfers.
Wave Burkina offers digital finance used for payment, money transfer and savings by traders, farmers and young entrepreneurs, per its representative at an ANPFI training launch.
leFaso.net says mobile money is in service in Burkina Faso, with Orange Money, Moov Money, Sank Money, Coris Money and Telecel Money all accepted by the YENGA app.
leFaso.net says the YENGA app, built by KREEZUS, sends money between different Mobile Money services in Burkina Faso, with over 400,000 downloads.
FinDev Gateway says social safety net beneficiaries in Burkina Faso receive and use mobile money accounts, with payments made to them since 2018.
L'Oeil du Sahel, citing BCEAO 2024 data, says Burkina Faso had 23,708,070 e-money accounts, 8,654,640 of them active, and 2,174,926,797 transactions in 2024.
